shouldFix.title: Retiring fixtureClassRides removed the only reporting slot for the AT-* acceptance classes, and fixtureMemberMap does not replace it, so the AT-8 and FG-7 obligations this revision adds cannot be recorded
detail: In v5 the report recorded coverage as { class: TC-* or AT-*, ... } and fixtureClassRides carried nine AT-* entries: AT-1-ASSEMBLY, AT-1-TRUSTED-INSTALL, AT-2, AT-3, AT-4, AT-5-ASSEMBLY, AT-5-TRUSTED-INSTALL, AT-6 and AT-7. Both halves are gone in v6. fixtureClassCoverage is now keyed strictly by 'memberKey: fixtureMemberMap key', and fixtureClassRides is reduced to two meta fields declaring the class strings retired.

fixtureMemberMap does not carry the AT-* half. I enumerated all 50 keys: every one is a TC-* member, and a search for keys beginning 'AT' returns none. So no AT-* class has any key that fixtureClassCoverage will accept.

That leaves this revision's own new obligations unrecordable. AT-8 requires 'Every archiveProfile.byteAlgorithm.goldenAndNegativeCases member' - eleven AT-ARCHIVE-* cases - and FG-7 states those cases 'are required AT-ARCHIVE-* members'. Neither AT-8 nor any AT-ARCHIVE-* case has a slot in the report shape.

It also strands the deferrals. lawfulExemptions now says not-applicable and blocked-on-ride are lawful 'only via the ride recorded on that memberKey', so with no AT-* memberKey an acceptance class cannot even be lawfully marked blocked-on-ride. AT-1-TRUSTED-INSTALL and AT-5-TRUSTED-INSTALL, which v5 explicitly parked on ID-DEP-P3, now have no way to say so.

The asymmetry with the TC-* half is what makes this visible: FG-6 makes a report invalid if it 'is missing any fixtureMemberMap key', so every TC-* member must appear, while no rule requires or even permits an AT-* row. AT-4's health half does land - healthAndSubprotocol.applicability is a closed record and I verified it - but AT-4's own pass/fail standing has nowhere to go.

I checked the rest of the report shape for a substitute and there is none: outputContractMembers is keyed by OC-1..OC-9, gateResults by DR-G* or DR-115/118, staticValidation by DR-103 refusal id or OC id. None accepts an AT id.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: CODEX-V4-S1 asked for member-level keying instead of class-level alternatives, and v6 delivers that for the schema classes with real rigour. But the repair was applied to only one of the two families the report covered, and the dropped family is the one carrying this artifact's own acceptance tests - including the archive golden and negative cases that are the entire evidentiary basis for the byteAlgorithm work this revision adds. As written, an adapter can emit a fully valid conformance report that says nothing about whether two adapters produced identical archive bytes, whether the 101-byte overflow refused, or whether trusted install is still parked.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing false is asserted and no authorization creeps. The AT-* classes still exist and state their requirements in /acceptanceTests/classes; what is missing is the report slot to record their standing. The fix is additive and follows the pattern already built.
shouldFix.remedy: Extend fixtureMemberMap with AT-* members under the same one-producer / one-expected discipline - including the eleven AT-ARCHIVE-* cases from byteAlgorithm.goldenAndNegativeCases and the two trusted-install halves parked on ID-DEP-P3 - or add a parallel acceptanceTestResults array to the report shape keyed by AT id with the same standing enum, evidence and ride rules.

repairVerification.finding: CLAUDE-V5-S1 - the chksum computation rule used a NUL in the eight-octet mask, and devmajor/devminor were stated two incompatible ways
repairVerification.howIChecked: Both halves are fixed and stated twice consistently. metadata.checksum now reads 'Computation: sum of all 512 header bytes with the eight chksum octets taken as ASCII space 0x20. Stored layout: six octal digits, NUL, space. The stored layout is not the computation mask.' byteAlgorithm.headerLayout.checksumComputation repeats it and adds 'A NUL in the mask is forbidden.' That is the POSIX rule exactly, and it names the confusion that produced the v5 error. metadata.devmajor and devminor now read 'octal7nul of 0 ... Empty-field alternative is forbidden', which agrees with numericFields and with headerLayout, where both fields are 'octal7nul of 0'. The ambiguity is gone in both directions.

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V4-B1 residue - POSIX ustar named as a family rather than a complete tree-to-byte algorithm
repairVerification.disposition: REPAIRED - VERIFIED, and I checked the layout arithmetic
repairVerification.howIChecked: archiveProfile.byteAlgorithm is a genuine algorithm, not a label. I verified the header layout field by field against the POSIX ustar block: name 0/100, mode 100/8, uid 108/8, gid 116/8, size 124/12, mtime 136/12, chksum 148/8, typeflag 156/1, linkname 157/100, magic 257/6, version 263/2, uname 265/32, gname 297/32, devmajor 329/8, devminor 337/8, prefix 345/155, pad 500/12 - every offset contiguous and summing to exactly 512. The four family ambiguities the dispatch names are each closed: typeflagBytes fixes 0x30/0x35/0x32 and forbids the alternate regular-file 0x00; prefix is 155 NUL and 'never used to split a path'; bodyRules bind the file body to exactly TreeCommitment.length bytes whose sha256 equals TreeCommitment.sha256 then NUL-pad to the 512 boundary, with the length-0 and exact-multiple cases called out; and the trailer is exactly two zero blocks with 'Physical blocking factor is 1 block' and 'Bytes after the two zero blocks do not exist.' PAX/GNU longname/longlink extensions are forbidden. The archiveLength formula '512 * N_members + sum over file members of 512*ceil(length/512) + 1024' follows from those rules and is correct, including the zero-length case. bijection and admissionChecks give the reader side.

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V4-B1 - the 100-byte capacity was a hidden cap not owned at OD-P2
repairVerification.howIChecked: OD-P2 gains profileCapacityDeclaredHere with standing 'DECLARED profile constraint, not a schema cap, not hidden', binding the name field to <= 100 UTF-8 bytes of the NFC path with typed non-success PATH-EXCEEDS-USTAR-NAME and the linkname field likewise with LINKTARGET-EXCEEDS-USTAR-LINKNAME. Its relationshipToOD1 states plainly that schemas.v11 OD-1 remains OPEN and UNSPECIFIED at admission, that a schema-valid tree may fail this profile, and that the refusal is owned here rather than being an implied OD-1 number. byteAlgorithm.doesNotMintSchemaCaps repeats it. The boundary between a profile capacity and a schema cap is now explicit rather than silent.

OD-P2.decision now reads 'Schema-level size caps (schemas.v11 OD-1: manifest byte size, tree entry count, path length, alias count)', owner reads 'Still schemas.v11 OD-1 ... This artifact does not mint schema caps', and a new doesNotPointAt field states 'historical schemas.v2. Live schema pin is schemas.v11.'

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V4-S1 - fixtureClassRides class-level alternatives standing in for member coverage
repairVerification.disposition: REPAIRED - VERIFIED, and I checked the map against the schema
repairVerification.howIChecked: I counted schemas.v11's testCorpusRequirements requires[] strings directly: TC-ACCEPT 6, TC-DUP 5, TC-NAME 12, TC-PATH 13, TC-SIG 2, TC-CLOSURE 3, TC-METADATA-ONLY 1, TC-BYTE-EXACT 3 - total 45. fixtureMemberMap declares schemaRequiresCount 45 and mapKeyCount 50, and both are exactly right: the map holds 50 members, and every one of the 45 requires strings is keyed with a requireVerbatim that matches the schema string byte for byte. The five extra keys are declared and correct - the TC-NAME.4 stale-alias require is split into TC-NAME.4.inside (expected ACCEPT) and TC-NAME.4.after (expected refuse:typed-stale-alias), which is the both-edges obligation the schema states in one string, and four conditional arms are added as TC-SIG.C-ENVELOPE, TC-SIG.C-LOCK, TC-BYTE-EXACT.C-CANON and TC-BYTE-EXACT.C-LOCK. I searched every member's producer field for a class-level alternative and found no 'or' and no '|' anywhere: each member has exactly one producer and one expected outcome. Members that cannot be produced carry producer 'none' with a named ride - TC-ACCEPT.5 the multi-component lock on ID-DEP-P2/DR-111, the two conditional TC-SIG arms, and the two TC-BYTE-EXACT arms. FG-1 is rewritten to be that map and FG-6 makes a report invalid on a missing key, duplicate key, class-wide stand-in, or a producer/ride other than the map entry.
repairVerification.residual: The same repair dropped the AT-* half of the coverage array. See V6-S1.

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V4-S2 - a health result could be omitted with no applicability standing
repairVerification.howIChecked: healthAndSubprotocol now carries a closed applicability record: an array of { role, platform, standing } over the enum executed-pass | executed-fail | not-applicable | blocked-on-ride, with { path, sha256 } REQUIRED for either executed standing and the AT-4 / ID-DEP-P4 ride REQUIRED for either deferred standing. 'A missing applicability array, or a member with no standing, is report-invalid' and 'Omission of healthResult without a ride is forbidden.' OC-6 carries the matching emission duty on both its emits and adapterDuty sides, and AT-4 is amended so that 'A report with no applicability record is AT-4 fail.' Omission is no longer silent.

attackListDisposition.attack: Checksum still computed with a NUL-in-mask
attackListDisposition.detail: Stated twice as all eight chksum octets at 0x20, with 'A NUL in the mask is forbidden' and the stored layout explicitly distinguished from the computation mask. AT-ARCHIVE-CHKSUM-SPACES exists as a negative case.

attackListDisposition.attack: POSIX ustar still a family (typeflag NUL, prefix split, unbound body, trailer pad)
attackListDisposition.detail: See CODEX-V4-B1 above. Typeflag bytes are exact and 0x00 is forbidden; prefix is 155 NUL and never splits; the body is bound to length and sha256 with a defined pad; the trailer is two blocks with blocking factor 1 and nothing after. encoding also forbids PAX/GNU longname/longlink and states 'One permitted byte representation.'

attackListDisposition.attack: Hidden path/link cap not owned at OD-P2
